title: NoteOn
tagline: Study great open lectures deeply, not just watch them.
summary: A personal study tool that puts a lecture video, Korean captions, timed key segments, sourced notes and your own memos on one screen.

problem: There are more excellent open lectures than ever, yet most of what I watched did not stay with me.
When a hard passage came up, the video, my notes and the sources that explained it lived in different tabs, and I lost the thread looking for them.
motivation: I wanted to understand lectures deeply and remember them, not let them stream past.
That needed two things: the evidence for a hard passage right beside the video, and a trace of my own thinking left on the sentence where it happened.
People now build personal tools for their own needs. NoteOn is mine: an interactive way to study, where I mark, annotate and come back.

features.title: Three ways in
features.text: Follow a course in order, jump straight to curated excerpts by topic, or browse and search in Korean and English.

features.title: Captions and key segments
features.text: Korean captions overlay the player; timed key segments sit beside it and start playback from that moment.

features.title: Notes that keep the video in view
features.text: Scroll into the notes and the player docks as a mini player above the contents. Each chapter carries a play range and its sources.

features.title: Sentence memos
features.text: Select sentences, even across paragraphs, and write a memo in your own words beside them. The selected text stays attached, and memos are private unless you choose to share them.

features.title: My study
features.text: Sign in with Google and the lectures you bookmark or like collect on one page, so you can pick up where you left off.
